pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is the strongest support. Revenue of USD 9,567.78 million in fiscal 2026 came almost entirely from federal agencies, backlog stood at USD 34.0 billion at 30 September 2026, and cost-plus contracts that pass cost increases to the customer supplied 56.0% of revenue, so demand and margin are well supported. Federal dependence also means no commercial customer can replace a lost agency, which is why funding timing, not demand, is the risk. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

Leverage is the main financial constraint. Total debt was 3.92x EBITDA and net debt 3.69x at 30 September 2026 on a last-twelve-months basis, against 3.02x and 2.91x at fiscal 2025 year-end, because the acquisition added debt before its earnings were fully counted. Cash interest cover of 5.60x flatters the current burden, since the September 2026 quarter's interest expense annualised gives 4.21x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1

Liquidity and the maturity profile leave no near-term refinancing pressure. Cash of USD 279.39 million plus USD 1,395.0 million of undrawn revolver gives USD 1,674.39 million against USD 46.75 million of principal scheduled for fiscal 2027, the revolver and term loan mature in November 2030, and the largest step, USD 1,706.75 million or 34.61% of principal, falls in fiscal 2031. The weakness is that the receivables-sale facility of up to USD 350.0 million has a stated term ending 18 December 2026 and its renewal is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 85, 89; calculation D1; calculation D2

Interest cost is the transmission channel from rates to cash flow. The floating-rate debt of USD 3,364.44 million is 41.61% covered by swaps of USD 1,400.0 million, and swaps of USD 350.0 million mature within twelve months, so each 100 bp move on the unhedged USD 1,964.44 million changes annual interest by about USD 19.64 million. That is small against EBITDA but compounds the leverage constraint if EBITDA stalls. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation D3; calculation D4

Cash conversion supports deleveraging if guidance is met. Operating cash flow excluding the receivables sale was 71.73% of fiscal 2026 EBITDA, and free cash flow over the last twelve months was 58.82% of EBITDA, so conversion is solid but was helped by lower cash taxes. Applying the guided USD 900 million of fiscal 2027 free cash flow to debt with EBITDA unchanged would bring net leverage from 3.69x to 2.96x, which is an illustration, not a forecast. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 11; calculation D5

Financial policy and governance are not the pressure point, but they are not established beyond the filings. No dividend or sponsor extraction is documented and repurchases are small, while acquisition appetite is the one behaviour that adds debt, and the executed debt documents that would show how far that can go are not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 88

runs.text: The first strength is a demand base that is large and spread across agencies with which the company has long-term relationships. Federal agencies supplied 95.6% of fiscal 2026 revenue and total backlog of USD 34.0 billion, with funded backlog at 18.24% of it, gives revenue visibility that a funding delay can postpone but not remove, which supports debt service through a cycle. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation K10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The second strength is liquidity and a long maturity profile. Liquidity of USD 1,674.39 million against fiscal 2027 principal of USD 46.75 million, and a revolver and term loan that run to November 2030, mean the first refinancing event is some years away and a funding disruption would be met from available cash and the revolver. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1

The third strength is cost pass-through and rising margin. Cost-plus-fee work was 56.0% of fiscal 2026 revenue and the EBITDA margin rose from 11.21% in fiscal 2025 to 12.65% over the last twelve months, which supports interest cover as the debt stack grows. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1

The fourth strength is financial policy that has not extracted cash. No dividend has ever been paid and repurchases fell sharply in fiscal 2026, so earnings have stayed available for debt service. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 67; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The first weakness is leverage after the acquisition. Total debt of 3.92x and net debt of 3.69x LTM EBITDA at 30 September 2026 are above the 3.02x and 2.91x of fiscal 2025 year-end, which reduces the cushion for creditors if earnings fall. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1

The second weakness is the dependence on federal funding timing. A continuing resolution funds the government to 11 December 2026 and a shutdown in the autumn of 2025 shows the risk is real, so a delay would hit awards and cash while debt service continues. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17

The third weakness is interest cost and hedge roll-off. Floating-rate debt is only 41.61% hedged and USD 350.0 million of swaps mature within twelve months, so a rate rise passes quickly into interest cost at a time when cover is already lower on an annualised basis. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation D3; calculation D4

The fourth weakness is acquisition appetite combined with slowing organic growth. Organic growth was 2.1% in the September 2026 quarter against 7.2% for fiscal 2026, so growth has relied on purchases that are funded with debt. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: ARKA Group L.P. was acquired on 9 March 2026 for USD 2,642.7 million net of cash acquired at 30 June 2026, later USD 2,637.7 million after a USD 5.0 million working-capital refund, and was funded from increased borrowings and cash on hand. The company had signed a commitment letter on 19 December 2025 for a senior secured bridge facility of up to USD 1,300.0 million, which stayed undrawn and ended on closing. The acquisition adds space-domain capability and, together with a smaller purchase, contributed USD 166.8 million of revenue in fiscal 2026. The pro forma results were judged not material by the company, so no combined earnings are available. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 79–81; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation K9

New debt was raised around the purchase. A Term Loan B-2 of USD 800.0 million, senior secured with guarantees and collateral identical to the existing Term Loan B, was added on 9 March 2026, and USD 500.0 million of additional 2033 senior unsecured notes were issued on 12 March 2026 at a premium for net proceeds of USD 516.5 million, used to repay revolver borrowings. The credit facility had been amended on 25 November 2025 to extend its maturity, with a revolver of USD 2,000.0 million and a term loan of USD 1,250.0 million, so the secured debt carries a majority of the company's assets as collateral while the notes sit behind it. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 88–89; 10-Q_2026-03-31_caci-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15

fields.value: The strongest evidence against reading leverage as still elevated is that the trailing figures carry the acquired business's debt for the whole period but only part of its earnings, since the acquisition closed on 9 March 2026 and no pro forma figures are supplied. A full-year earnings figure for the acquired business would lower both leverage ratios, and the company's guidance of at least USD 900 million of free cash flow for fiscal 2027, set against USD 725.96 million over the last twelve months, would cut net debt faster if delivered. The view would worsen if the receivables-sale facility lapsed without replacement, because up to USD 350.0 million of financing would leave the liquidity position, or if quarterly EBITDA stopped growing while cash interest stayed near its current level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CACI is a diversified but federally dependent contractor with no sponsor or controlling owner disclosed in the supplied filings, so creditor risk rests on acquisition appetite and government funding timing, not on sponsor behaviour.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Federal agencies supply 95.6% of revenue and the largest customer group, the Department of War, supplies 53.6%. Two debt-funded acquisitions in two years, USD 1,681.9 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 2,642.7 million for ARKA in fiscal 2026, show a financial policy that favours growth by purchase over shareholder distributions, and the company has never paid a cash dividend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is concentrated in one customer but spread across agencies, which makes cash timing the main business risk rather than demand. Federal contracts supplied 95.6% of fiscal 2026 revenue, the Department of War 53.6% and the intelligence community 24.6%, and the ten largest contracts supplied 22.5% of revenue, or USD 2.2 billion, so no single program dominates. Continuing resolutions and shutdowns delay new programs and awards, and the government can terminate contracts for convenience, so a funding gap hits revenue timing and cash before it hits underlying demand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The contract mix is moving toward fixed-price work, which raises margin potential and cost-overrun risk together. Fixed-price contracts supplied 30.4% of fiscal 2026 revenue against 26.3% a year earlier, and 33.2% in the September 2026 quarter against 26.7% a year earlier, while cost-plus-fee contracts fell from 60.5% to 56.0% for the year and to 52.8% in the quarter. Direct costs fell to 64.6% of revenue in the quarter from 67.6%, which the company attributes to a favourable revenue mix, so the margin gain is the visible reward and an overrun on a fixed-price program is the exposure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Backlog is large but only a small part is funded, and organic growth has slowed. Total backlog was USD 34.0 billion at 30 September 2026 and funded backlog USD 6.2 billion, 18.24% of the total, up from 15.93% a year earlier. Organic growth was 2.1% in the September 2026 quarter against 7.2% for fiscal 2026, so most of the quarter's 8.2% revenue growth came from acquisitions, while Department of War revenue rose 14.8% and federal civilian revenue fell 3.7%.

fields.value: Acquisition appetite is the main financial-policy signal, and it has been funded with debt. The company completed eight acquisitions in three fiscal years, three in fiscal 2025 for USD 1,681.9 million and ARKA in fiscal 2026 for USD 2,642.7 million net of cash acquired, funded from increased borrowings and cash, while principal debt rose by USD 1,988.50 million in fiscal 2026. Share repurchases fell from USD 168.56 million in fiscal 2025 to USD 17.08 million in fiscal 2026, which is consistent with cash being directed to acquisitions and debt service, and USD 187.3 million of the repurchase authorization remained at 30 September 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership and governance cannot be read as a sponsor case. The company is listed in New York with a small number of record holders, has never paid a cash dividend, and states a policy of retaining earnings, so no distribution or sponsor extraction is documented. The percentage held by any holder, the board's independence, related-party dealings and compensation sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so those questions are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure quality is good on the financial statements but thin on creditor protections. The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and found internal control effective, quarterly results are published within about three weeks of quarter end and annual results within about five weeks, and the debt note prints every instrument, but covenant levels, guarantor names and the legal ranking among secured facilities are not printed. A creditor can therefore monitor performance well and cannot test the debt documents' limits on further borrowing or distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A long-running civil action turned in the company's favour in October 2026 but is not finally closed. A jury verdict of USD 42 million in November 2024 was affirmed on appeal in March 2026, no amount was ever recognized, the Fourth Circuit directed dismissal in August 2026, and on 21 October 2026 the District Court vacated the judgment and dismissed the case, while the plaintiffs have said they may seek Supreme Court review. The amount is small against the company's liquidity, so the creditor consequence is limited to a tail risk and a second stayed suit that the District Court will dismiss or hold according to what the plaintiffs do.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against concern about acquisition-funded leverage is that the acquired businesses are being absorbed while the company still grew organically, margins widened and funded backlog rose, and that no distribution, waiver or exchange has been documented. If the company disclosed a leverage target, stated that further large purchases are paused until a ratio is reached, or supplied the debt documents showing tight limits on new debt and distributions, the view would move toward lower governance risk. The view would worsen if organic growth stayed near the September 2026 quarter's 2.1% while another debt-funded purchase was announced, or if the continuing resolution that funds the government to 11 December 2026 lapsed into a shutdown that delayed awards.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ARKA Group L.P. was acquired on 9 March 2026 for USD 2,642.7 million net of cash acquired at 30 June 2026, later USD 2,637.7 million after a USD 5.0 million working-capital refund, and was funded from increased borrowings and cash on hand. The company had signed a commitment letter on 19 December 2025 for a senior secured bridge facility of up to USD 1,300.0 million, which stayed undrawn and ended on closing. The acquisition adds space-domain capability and, together with a smaller purchase, contributed USD 166.8 million of revenue in fiscal 2026. The pro forma results were judged not material by the company, so no combined earnings are available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt was raised around the purchase. A Term Loan B-2 of USD 800.0 million, senior secured with guarantees and collateral identical to the existing Term Loan B, was added on 9 March 2026, and USD 500.0 million of additional 2033 senior unsecured notes were issued on 12 March 2026 at a premium for net proceeds of USD 516.5 million, used to repay revolver borrowings. The credit facility had been amended on 25 November 2025 to extend its maturity, with a revolver of USD 2,000.0 million and a term loan of USD 1,250.0 million, so the secured debt carries a majority of the company's assets as collateral while the notes sit behind it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, the company presents medium governance and sponsor risk. The key supported behaviour is repeated debt-funded acquisition, which matters because leverage rises before acquired earnings arrive and implies higher refinancing exposure, while no distribution or sponsor extraction is documented. Countervailing evidence is continued organic growth, a larger funded backlog and a large undrawn revolver, and further analysis requires the debt documents and the proxy statement. The governance and sponsor assessment is completed with limitations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CACI's fundamental credit profile is adequate: durable federal demand and USD 1,674.39 million of liquidity support creditors, but leverage of 3.92x after a debt-funded acquisition and dependence on federal funding timing mean deleveraging must come from free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main downside path is a federal funding disruption after the continuing resolution ends on 11 December 2026, delaying awards while debt service and the floating-rate cost of the acquisition debt continue. Free cash flow of USD 725.96 million over the last twelve months is 58.82% of EBITDA, and the company's guidance of at least USD 900 million for fiscal 2027 would speed repayment if met.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation D1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is the strongest support. Revenue of USD 9,567.78 million in fiscal 2026 came almost entirely from federal agencies, backlog stood at USD 34.0 billion at 30 September 2026, and cost-plus contracts that pass cost increases to the customer supplied 56.0% of revenue, so demand and margin are well supported. Federal dependence also means no commercial customer can replace a lost agency, which is why funding timing, not demand, is the risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the main financial constraint. Total debt was 3.92x EBITDA and net debt 3.69x at 30 September 2026 on a last-twelve-months basis, against 3.02x and 2.91x at fiscal 2025 year-end, because the acquisition added debt before its earnings were fully counted. Cash interest cover of 5.60x flatters the current burden, since the September 2026 quarter's interest expense annualised gives 4.21x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the maturity profile leave no near-term refinancing pressure. Cash of USD 279.39 million plus USD 1,395.0 million of undrawn revolver gives USD 1,674.39 million against USD 46.75 million of principal scheduled for fiscal 2027, the revolver and term loan mature in November 2030, and the largest step, USD 1,706.75 million or 34.61% of principal, falls in fiscal 2031. The weakness is that the receivables-sale facility of up to USD 350.0 million has a stated term ending 18 December 2026 and its renewal is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 85, 89; calculation D1; calculation D2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cost is the transmission channel from rates to cash flow. The floating-rate debt of USD 3,364.44 million is 41.61% covered by swaps of USD 1,400.0 million, and swaps of USD 350.0 million mature within twelve months, so each 100 bp move on the unhedged USD 1,964.44 million changes annual interest by about USD 19.64 million. That is small against EBITDA but compounds the leverage constraint if EBITDA stalls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation D3; calculation D4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion supports deleveraging if guidance is met. Operating cash flow excluding the receivables sale was 71.73% of fiscal 2026 EBITDA, and free cash flow over the last twelve months was 58.82% of EBITDA, so conversion is solid but was helped by lower cash taxes. Applying the guided USD 900 million of fiscal 2027 free cash flow to debt with EBITDA unchanged would bring net leverage from 3.69x to 2.96x, which is an illustration, not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 11; calculation D5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy and governance are not the pressure point, but they are not established beyond the filings. No dividend or sponsor extraction is documented and repurchases are small, while acquisition appetite is the one behaviour that adds debt, and the executed debt documents that would show how far that can go are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a stronger credit view is that leverage fell from 4.18x at fiscal 2026 year-end to 3.92x within a quarter, that earnings of the acquired business are only partly counted so true run-rate leverage is lower, and that the backlog and margin trend are rising. The strongest evidence for a weaker view is that organic growth slowed to 2.1% in the September 2026 quarter and interest expense on an annualised basis implies cover of 4.21x. The view would improve if full-year earnings of the acquired business or covenant levels showed sufficient headroom, and worsen if the continuing resolution lapsed into a shutdown, the receivables-sale facility were not renewed, or a further debt-funded purchase were announced before leverage returned toward the fiscal 2025 level of 3.02x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit ratings, peer data or market quotes are supplied, so the profile cannot be set against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector and no rating view is given; the conclusion is absolute, not relative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels and the legal terms of the debt are not supplied, so the liquidity and leverage conclusions say nothing about headroom or capacity to add debt, and the financial policy assessment is behavioural only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside path is qualitative and anchored on observed levels, because no source gives a stress threshold; the size of a funding disruption on cash flow is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Pro forma earnings for the acquired business are not supplied, so the leverage ratios are stated as reported and the extent to which they overstate run-rate leverage is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is a demand base that is large and spread across agencies with which the company has long-term relationships. Federal agencies supplied 95.6% of fiscal 2026 revenue and total backlog of USD 34.0 billion, with funded backlog at 18.24% of it, gives revenue visibility that a funding delay can postpone but not remove, which supports debt service through a cycle.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation K10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is liquidity and a long maturity profile. Liquidity of USD 1,674.39 million against fiscal 2027 principal of USD 46.75 million, and a revolver and term loan that run to November 2030, mean the first refinancing event is some years away and a funding disruption would be met from available cash and the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is cost pass-through and rising margin. Cost-plus-fee work was 56.0% of fiscal 2026 revenue and the EBITDA margin rose from 11.21% in fiscal 2025 to 12.65% over the last twelve months, which supports interest cover as the debt stack grows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth strength is financial policy that has not extracted cash. No dividend has ever been paid and repurchases fell sharply in fiscal 2026, so earnings have stayed available for debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is leverage after the acquisition. Total debt of 3.92x and net debt of 3.69x LTM EBITDA at 30 September 2026 are above the 3.02x and 2.91x of fiscal 2025 year-end, which reduces the cushion for creditors if earnings fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is the dependence on federal funding timing. A continuing resolution funds the government to 11 December 2026 and a shutdown in the autumn of 2025 shows the risk is real, so a delay would hit awards and cash while debt service continues.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is interest cost and hedge roll-off. Floating-rate debt is only 41.61% hedged and USD 350.0 million of swaps mature within twelve months, so a rate rise passes quickly into interest cost at a time when cover is already lower on an annualised basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation D3; calculation D4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is acquisition appetite combined with slowing organic growth. Organic growth was 2.1% in the September 2026 quarter against 7.2% for fiscal 2026, so growth has relied on purchases that are funded with debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CACI provides technology and expertise to national security customers in intelligence, defense and federal civilian agencies through a holding company with subsidiaries in the United States and Europe. Domestic Operations produced 96.8% of fiscal 2026 revenue, and the company grew through eight acquisitions in three fiscal years, the largest being ARKA in March 2026, which adds space-domain capability. Cash-flow visibility comes from long, multi-year contracts and a large backlog, so debt service is supported, while refinancing confidence depends on continued federal funding because no commercial customer base offsets it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CACI International Inc is a listed holding company with no sponsor or controlling holder disclosed in the supplied documents, so there is no sponsor whose willingness to support or extract cash needs to be judged. Debt is issued or borrowed at the holding company with guarantors that are not named, which means structural priority cannot be read from the filings and is passed to the module that handles it. The financial policy evidence is a record of debt-funded acquisition, no dividend and falling repurchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable but concentrated rather than recurring in the commercial sense. Federal agencies supplied 95.6% of revenue, the ten largest contracts 22.5%, and the company wins work by competitive bid, so growth comes from new awards and exercised options and not from pricing power. Total backlog includes unexercised options and only USD 6.2 billion is funded, so revenue beyond the funded work depends on appropriations, and organic growth of 2.1% in the latest quarter shows demand is steady rather than accelerating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are defended by contract structure but exposed to the shift to fixed-price work. Direct costs of 66.80% of fiscal 2026 revenue are largely labour and subcontractors that cost-plus contracts pass through, which protects margin when volumes or wages move, while fixed-price work rose from 26.3% to 30.4% of revenue and to 33.2% in the latest quarter, so the company now carries more overrun risk for a higher margin. EBITDA grew 21.42% in fiscal 2026 against revenue growth of 10.89%, which shows operating leverage working upward and would work downward if revenue stalled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 52, 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital needs are light and cash conversion is the main support for deleveraging. Capital expenditure was 1.11% of fiscal 2026 revenue, so most operating cash flow is available for debt service, and free cash flow over the last twelve months was 58.82% of EBITDA. Cash interest and acquisition-related integration costs absorb the rest, and cash taxes fell in fiscal 2026, which means part of the conversion may not repeat.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation D1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high because essentially all contracts allow the government to terminate for convenience, and the customer sets contract terms, so a lost recompete removes revenue without recourse. Rivalry is intense with larger competitors and non-traditional entrants in cloud, cyber and satellite operations, which pressures pricing at recompete, while indirect competition from agencies doing work in-house limits the addressable market. Supplier power cannot be sized because subcontractor cost sits inside direct costs, but cleared labour is scarce, which raises wage cost, and in 9.91% of revenue the company is itself a subcontractor, so a prime contractor's cash problems can reach it; the threat of substitution appears low for classified mission work.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Federal budget policy is the one macro factor that changes credit quality. Continuing resolutions delay new programs and awards, the reconciliation law made about USD 156 billion of defense funding available regardless of annual appropriations, and the government is funded only to 11 December 2026, so a lapse would test liquidity while longer-term funding looks supported. Interest rates matter through the floating-rate debt, and technology change is a revenue driver rather than a credit threat in the period reviewed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are the funded federal demand, backlog, cost pass-through and liquidity described above. Weaknesses are post-acquisition leverage, dependence on one customer, the fixed-price shift and interest cost. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are guided free cash flow of at least USD 900 million, margin expansion and conversion of the acquired space business into earnings that lower leverage. Threats that could weaken it are a funding lapse, a further debt-funded acquisition, non-renewal of the receivables-sale facility and loss of a large recompete.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is adequate and trending toward better leverage but not yet there. Scale is large with revenue of USD 9,567.78 million, margin is rising, liquidity is USD 1,674.39 million, and conversion supports repayment, while leverage of 3.92x and the cost of floating-rate debt constrain it. Refinancing capacity looks sound for the next several years because the nearest large maturity is in fiscal 2031, though capital-market access is judged only from that profile because ratings and market prices are not supplied. The missing datapoints that would sharpen the view are covenant levels, pro forma earnings and ratings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1; calculation D8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For the next twelve to twenty-four months the company guides fiscal 2027 revenue of USD 10,700 million to USD 10,900 million, which implies growth of 11.83% to 13.92% over fiscal 2026 once the full year of the acquired business is included, and free cash flow of at least USD 900 million. Tailwinds are the backlog, a 2.0x book-to-bill in the latest quarter, Department of War revenue growth of 14.8% and mandatory defense funding; headwinds are the 3.7% fall in federal civilian revenue, slowing organic growth and the funding lapse risk. Medium-term outlook over three to five years is not established, because the company states targets without figures in the supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a federal funding lapse when the continuing resolution ends on 11 December 2026. The first operational break is delayed new awards and program starts, which would slow growth beyond the 2.1% organic rate and could slow collections, since days sales outstanding already rose to 59 days. The financial transmission is lower operating cash flow while cash interest and scheduled principal continue, and if the receivables-sale facility were not renewed after 18 December 2026 up to USD 350.0 million of financing would need replacing. The liquidity consequence is a draw on the revolver from USD 605.00 million, but liquidity of USD 1,674.39 million is 4.78 times that facility, so the scenario does not point to liquidity distress, and leverage would rise only through lower EBITDA. Management levers are cutting acquisitions, repurchases and capital expenditure, and the observable triggers are the funding status after 11 December, revolver drawings and the receivables-sale renewal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, CACI presents a business profile that is large and supported by funded federal demand, but credit quality is constrained by leverage after a debt-funded acquisition. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to cost pass-through, light capital needs and a rising margin. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the next two to three years of free cash flow and on the November 2030 maturities. The primary downside path is a federal funding disruption that delays awards while interest on partly unhedged floating-rate debt continues. Further analysis would require covenant levels, pro forma earnings for the acquired business, and ratings and market prices. Top risk: federal funding timing.
